GEB121.rationale: GEB ও বায়োটেকনোলজির মৌলিক ধারণা এবং বিভিন্ন ক্ষেত্রে এর প্রয়োগের পরিধি জানানোই এই কোর্সের লক্ষ্য।
objectives: বায়োটেকনোলজির মৌলিক ধারণা দেওয়া
খাতভিত্তিক (sector-wise) প্রয়োগ বুঝতে শেখানো
বায়োটেকনোলজিক্যাল প্রয়োগে সেফটি-সংক্রান্ত বিষয়ে সচেতন করা

contents.t: Definition of Biotechnology, history and multidisciplinary nature, applications, biotechnology and developing countries, commercialization of biotechnology in a developing country.
Concepts of rDNA technology, biological tools of rDNA technology, modification of the gene, methods of gene transfer, transgenic organisms.

Definition and history of medical biotechnology, drug discovery, pharmacology and pharmacogenomics, gene therapy, stem cell, tissue engineering, genetic testing, production of vaccines, commercial chemicals and antibiotics, application in forensics.

Definition and timeline of food biotechnology, old versus new techniques, importance and potential applications, threats and the double side of GM food, consumer benefit, food safety and sustainability, dairy / fish / meat products, food enzymes, sweeteners, oriental fermented foods, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, food wastes, microbial food products.

Impact of biotechnology in agriculture, biotechnological products from plants and crops and their uses, methods used in crop production, genetic manipulation of plants, biofertilizer, biopesticides, biocontrol of weeds, plant tissue culture and its application.
Animal wealth, products from animals, biotechnological methods in animal production, genetic manipulation of animals, biopharmaceuticals and blood substitutes from transgenic animals.
Definition; application of microbial biotechnology in industry and health science.

Definition of enzyme, enzymology and enzyme technology, comparison between enzyme and catalyst, nature of enzymes, therapeutic / analytical / manipulative / industrial uses, application of GEB in enzyme production, immobilized enzymes.
Photosynthesis as the ultimate energy resource, sources of biomass, ethanol from biomass, methane from biomass, biogas production.
Concepts of biosafety, sources of environmental pollution, commercial blends of microorganisms and enzymes in pollution control, biotechnological approaches in waste treatment.
Concepts, scope, importance and applications of bioinformatics; definition, scope and applications of biosensors; definition, application and future research trend of nanobiotechnology.

cos: Understand the multidisciplinary nature and applications of biotechnology
Understand key techniques in recombinant DNA technology
Apply biotechnology applications in various fields
Explore emerging areas and ethical considerations in biotechnology

ANS123.rationale: জীবন, প্রাণিজগৎ ও তাদের জীববিজ্ঞান, বাস্তুবিদ্যা, অর্থনীতি ও স্বাস্থ্য সম্পর্কে তাত্ত্বিক জ্ঞান — বায়োটেকনোলজিক্যাল প্রয়োগের ভিত্তি হিসেবে।
objectives: জীবন সম্পর্কে ধারণা
প্রাণীর বৈচিত্র্য ও সিস্টেম্যাটিক্স
প্রাণীর মৌলিক মরফোলজি ও গঠন
মডেল অ্যানিম্যাল পরিচিতি
অর্থনৈতিকভাবে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রাণী
অ্যানিম্যাল ইকোলজি ও ম্যানেজমেন্ট
গৃহপালিত প্রাণীর স্বাস্থ্য
মানুষ ও মানব-জীববিজ্ঞান

contents.t: Definition of life, theory of life, origin of life.
Definition of animal, animal kingdom and diversity, economic importance, classification.
Comparative anatomy (skeletal, circulatory, digestive, respiratory, excretory, reproductive systems) of human, cattle, goat etc.

Habitat, distribution, external morphology, organ systems, economic and biotechnological significance of Macrobrachium rosenbergii (Arthropoda), Lamellidens sp. (Mollusca), Labeo rohita (Pisces), Gallus domesticus (Aves), Cattle and Goat (Mammalia).
Animals used in laboratory for practical and research purposes.
Definition, branches, ecosystem, relationship of ecology with other disciplines; effect of environment and human habitation on adaptation.
Apiculture, sericulture, poultry and dairy farming — technical, commercial and financial aspects.

Microbial (viral, bacterial, fungal), parasitic (protozoan, helminth, arthropod), metabolic and nutritional diseases of poultry and dairy animals: etiology, pathogenesis, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, control.
Human type and race, different systems, food and nutrition, environmental stress and plasticity, disease and health management, demography and family planning.

cos: Recognize the basic concepts of life, value of animal resources, biodiversity
Understand anatomy, biology, ecology and management of important animals
Use economically important animals for commercial product development
Apply model animals in biomedical research
Manage health condition of farm animals and human life for biomedical applications

খামার ও বন্য প্রাণী উৎপাদনের মৌলিক জ্ঞান
মডেল অ্যানিম্যালের কালচার

PLS125.rationale: উদ্ভিদ জীববিজ্ঞান, অর্থনৈতিক গুরুত্ব এবং বৃদ্ধি ও বিকাশের প্রধান ফিজিওলজিক্যাল প্রক্রিয়াগুলো বোঝার জন্য প্রস্তুত করা।
objectives: উদ্ভিদ কোষ, টিস্যু, অঙ্গ, ফিজিওলজি, প্রজনন ও বৈচিত্র্যের মূলনীতি
কৃষি ও ঔষধি ফসলের সুযোগ ও ক্যারিয়ার সম্ভাবনা
মেটাবলিজম, সালোকসংশ্লেষণ ও হরমোনের ধারণা
উদ্ভিদের অঙ্গ, ফুল-বীজ, পুষ্টি উপাদান ও আলোর ভূমিকা

contents.t: The plant kingdom, importance of plant science, basic ideas of agronomy, horticulture, pomology, olericulture.
Seed and seedling; shoot, root, inflorescence and bracts, flower, leaves, buds; pollination, fertilization, embryology, fruits, disposal of fruits and seeds.
Outline of plant body: axis, primary and secondary body; cell structure and components, cell wall, mitosis, amitosis, meiosis and its significance.
Cereals, fibers, oils, fruits, rubber, beverage, sugar, fodder, pulse, timber and narcotic-yielding plants; cultivation and processing of tea and rubber.
Importance of medicinal plants, available components and their application in different diseases.

Inhibition, diffusion, osmosis, osmotic pressure, plasmolysis, imbibition, colloid, root pressure; absorption (active/passive), conduction and translocation; transpiration, guttation, stomatal mechanism.
Essential elements, source, functions of micro and macro elements, deficiency symptoms, absorption and translocation of mineral salts.
Pigments, light and dark reactions, photophosphorylation, C3 / C4 / CAM pathways, source–sink; respiration pathways, fermentation, ATP, photorespiration.
Growth concepts, sigmoid curve, differentiation, senescence; auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid, ethylene, growth retardants.
Florigen, photoperiodism and vernalization, phytochrome and blue-light photoreceptors, photomorphogenesis, biological clocks.

cos: Describe the diversity of plant form and function, expression and inheritance of traits
Recognize the economic importance of cereals, vegetables, fruits and medicinal plants
Communicate the importance of plant science in addressing societal challenges
Develop personal skills to conduct plant science and physiological research
Contribute to plant-based pharmaceuticals and industry

ডিফিউশন, অসমোসিস, ট্রান্সপিরেশন, ফটোপিরিয়ডিজম ইত্যাদি এক্সপেরিমেন্টে শেখা

contents.t: Identification of lab specimens, plant cell structure and organelles; plant body, flower and fruit; morphology of rice, wheat, sugarcane, tobacco, lentil, nut, cotton, jute etc.; economic and medicinal plants and isolated compounds; experiments on diffusion, osmosis, osmotic pressure, plasmolysis, imbibition; starch test on leaf and seed; transpiration and guttation; essential elements; seed germination and viability test.

cos: Explain common research techniques in plant science and physiology
Interpret basic mechanisms of plant physiological processes
Explain plant growth, development and interaction with environment
Recognize seed germination and viability tests

MCB127.rationale: অণুজীব সম্পর্কে মৌলিক জ্ঞান (বিশেষত ব্যাকটেরিয়া) এবং মাইক্রোবায়োলজির মৌলিক ধারণা ও দক্ষতা অর্জন।
objectives: মৌলিক মাইক্রোবায়োলজিক্যাল নীতি
অণুজীব জগতের সদস্য ও GEB-তে তাদের ভূমিকা
বিভিন্ন অণুজীবের মাইক্রোস্কোপি
Taxonomy, sterilization, disinfection, growth ও culture methodology

contents.t: Microorganism and microbiology; place in living world; history (early observations, spontaneous generation debate, germ theory, vaccination, antibiotics); modern developments; scope.
Bacteria, archaebacteria, rickettsia, mycoplasma, actinomycetes, fungi, algae, protozoa, virus, viroids, prions; classification based on temperature, pH, oxygen, salinity, nutrients and pressure.
Capsule, flagella, pili, cell wall, cytoplasmic membrane, inclusion bodies, ribosome, pigments, endospore; classification; multiplication; economic importance.
Simple, defined, complex, selective, differential and enrichment media; batch and continuous culture; anaerobic culture methods; culture preservation.
Nutritional and physical requirements, growth curve, measurement of growth, growth equation.
Principles and methods of sterilization; effect of antimicrobial agents.
Ecology and ecosystem; biotic and abiotic factors; microbes in soil, air, water; neutralism, synergism, mutualism, commensalism, antagonism, parasitism, predation.
Morphological, cultural, biochemical, serological and molecular techniques.

cos: Recognize the importance of microorganisms in GEB
Recognize diversity of microorganisms and microbial communities
Interpret structural similarities/differences among prokaryotic and eukaryotic microbes
Identify structure–function relationships of bacterial cells and viruses
Design culture media and methods for growth; control and maintain microorganisms safely
refs: Pelczar, Chan & Krieg (1993) Microbiology. McGraw Hill
Tortora, Funke & Case (1982) Microbiology: An Introduction
Stanier, Adelberg & Ingraham. General Microbiology. Macmillan
Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg (1991) Medical Microbiology

objectives: মাইক্রোবিয়াল টেকনিকের মৌলিক টুল চেনা
অ্যাসেপটিক, স্টেরিলাইজেশন ও কালচার টেকনিক
ব্যাকটেরিয়া ও ছত্রাকের আইসোলেশন ও আইডেন্টিফিকেশন
প্যাথোজেনের অ্যান্টিমাইক্রোবিয়াল অ্যাক্টিভিটি বিশ্লেষণ

contents.t: 1) Handling and use of microscopes. 2) Sterilization: dry heat, moist heat, filtration. 3) Enumeration of bacterial counts by spread plate and pour plate. 4) Pure culture by streak plate. 5) Cultural characteristics on nutrient agar, selective and differential media. 6) Gram staining technique.

Prepare different culture media
Perform staining techniques
Measure bacterial growth and perform antibiotic susceptibility test
Identify and manage biohazards

GEB 0512 1121.rationale: The course is designed to provide the fundamental concepts of Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (GEB) and its scope of application in various fields of biotechnology.
objectives: To provide basic concepts in Biotechnology
To acquire Interpreting of sector-wise application of Biotechnology
To get acquainted with safety concerns in Biotechnological applications

Course Contents Concept: Definition of Biotechnology, history and multidisciplinary nature of Biotechnology, applications of Biotechnology, Biotechnology and developing countries, commercialization of Biotechnology in a developing country.
Recombinant DNA Technology: Concepts of Recombinant DNA technology, biological tools of Recombinant DNA technology, modification of the gene, methods of gene transfer, transgenic organisms.

Biotechnology in Medicine: Definition of medical biotechnology, History of medical biotechnology, application of medical biotechnology in drug discovery, pharmacology and pharmacogenomics, gene therapy, stem cell, tissue engineering, genetc testing, production of vaccines, commercial chemicals, and antibiotics, application of biotechnology in forensics.

Biotechnology in Food: Definition of food biotechnology, food biotechnology timeline, old versus new techniques in food biotechnology, importance of food biotechnology, potential application of food biotechnology in food safety, sustainability, consumer benefit and feeding a hungry world, possible threats of food biotechnology, double side of GMO, application of biotechnology in dairy products, fish and meat products, food enzymes, sweeteners, bakery products, food wastes, microbial products, oriental fermented foods, drinks, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages.

Biotechnology in Plant and Agriculture: Impact of Biotechnology in Agriculture, list of biotechnological products produced from plant and crops and their uses, biotechnological methods used in crop production, genetic manipulation of the plant, biofertilizer, biopesticide, biocontrol of weeds, plant tissue culture its application.

Biotechnology in Animal Production: Animal wealth, products from animal, biotechnological methods used in animal production, genetic manipulation of animal, animal cell culture, pharmaceuticals from transgenic animals, blood substitutes from transgenic animals.
Microbial Biotechnology: Definition, application of microbial biotechnology in industry and health science.

Enzymology and Enzyme Technology: Definition of enzyme, enzymology and enzyme technology, comparision between enzyme and catalyst, nature of the enzymes, applications of enzymes in therapeutic uses, analytical uses, manipulative uses and industrial uses, application of GEB in enzyme production, application of immobilized enzymes.
Biological Fuel Generation: Photosynthesis- ultimate energy resources, sources of biomass, ethanol from biomass, methane from biomass, biogas production.

Biosafety and Environmental Biotechnology: Concepts of bio safety, Sources of environmental pollution, use of commercial blends of microorganism and enzymes in pollution control. Biotechnological approaches in waste treatment.
Bioinformatics: Concepts, scope, importance and applications of bioinformatics.
Biosensor: Definition of biosensor, scope and applications.
Nanobiotechnology: Definintion, application, and future research treand.

Understand Key Techniques in Recombinant DNA Technology.
Apply Biotechnology Applications in Various Fields.
Explore Emerging Areas and Ethical Considerations in Biotechnology.

ANS 0511 1123.rationale: The course provides theoretical knowledge to the students in the area of life, animal kingdom and their biology, ecology, economy, health etc. for biotechnological applications.
objectives: To understand the things about the life
To familiarize the students with states of animals with diversity and systematics
To understand basic morphology and structural architecture of animals
To introduce about model animals
To provide knowledge about economically important animals
To acquire preliminary ideas about animal ecology and management
To accumulate basic ideas about health conditions of domestic animals
Acquainted with the human being and human biology

contents.t: Definition of life, theory of life, origin of life etc. Diversity of animals: Definition of animal, introduction to animal, animal kingdom and diversity, economic importance of animals, classification of animmal. Anatomy of Higher Animals: Comparative anatomy (Skeletal, circulatory, digestive, respiratory, excretory and reproductive systems) of higher animals (Human, Cattle, Goat, etc). Type Study of Animals: Type study including habitat, distribution, external morphology, organ system, the economic and biotechnological significance of the following: Arthropoda (Macrobrachium rosenbergii), Mollusca (Lamellidens sp.), Pisces (Labeo rohita ), Aves (Gallus domesticus) and Mammalia (Cattle and Goat). Laboratory Animals: Different animals used in the laboratory for practical and research purposes. Animal Ecology: Definition, branches, ecosystem, the relationship of ecology with another discipline. Effect of environment and human habitation on animal adaptation and their relationship with civilization. Economic Study of Animals: Apiculture, sericulture, poultry and dairy farming including technical, commercial and financial aspects. Major Diseases of Animals: Major Microbial (Viral, bacterial, fungal), Parasitic (protozoan, helminth, arthropod) Metabolic and Nutritional diseases of poultry birds, dairy animals with their causal agents, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical symptoms, diagnosis, treatment and control measures. Human Biology: Human type and race, Different systems, Food and nutrition, Environmental stress and Plasticity, Disease and Health Management, Demography and Family Planning.

cos: Recognize the basic concepts of life, the value of animal resources, biodiversity
Understand the anatomy, biology, ecology and management of importan animals.
Use of economically important animals for the development of commercial products
Apply model animals in biomedical research
Manage the health condition of farm animals as well as human life for biomedical applications

objectives: To achieve the practical knowledge of wildlife and domestic animals
To familiarize of animals and their body parts
To understand external morphology and internal structure of animals
To accumulate basic ideas about pathogens and control measures of diseases
To gain fundamental knowledge for production of farm and wild animals
To understand the culture practice of model animals

Field visit, sample collection and preservation
Spot identification including whole animals, parts of animals and slide of different invertebrates and vertebrates
External morphology of different invertebrates and vertebrates
Internal anatomy of different invertebrates and vertebrates
Study of parasites
Study of articulated bone
Slide mounting
Culture practice of model animals including C. elegance, Drosophila, Daphnia, Cyclops, Rotifer, Artemia, Zebra Fish, Mouse etc. in a laboratory setup

Identify the economic traits of animals and hand on experiences on restraining of animals
Gain knowledge on culture practice of economically important animals
Identify the health condition, pathogens and diseases of farm and wild animals
Recognize the diversity, habit and habitats of animals

PLS 0511 1125.rationale: The purpose of this course is to prepare students with specific competencies for fundamental understanding of plant biology, economic importance and major physiological processes which occur during plant growth and development as well as their interaction with the external environment.
objectives: To familiarize the basic principles of plant cells and tissues; plant organs; plant physiology; plant reproduction and diversity; and plant ecology.
To assess future agriculturally important crops, medicinally important crops, their production needs and opportunities to identify potential career paths in the agricultural sciences.
To build a clear concept on different biochemical processes like metabolism, photosynthesis and hormonal contribution towards plant growth.

To teach thoroughly about all the organs and parts of plants including flower and seed, necessary elements required to grow plants, how plants absorb these elements and the role of light in plants life.

The seed and seedling, The plant body – The shoot, the root, the inflorescence and bracts, the flower, the leaves, the buds, Pollination, Fertilization, embryology, the fruits, disposal of fruits and seeds.

contents.h: Plant Anatomy- An outline of the plant body

Introduction and scope of economic plants, scientific name, local name, useful parts and economic importance of cereals, fibers, oils, fruits, rubber, beverage, sugar, fodder, pulse, timber and narcotic yielding plants, cultivation and processing of tea and rubber plants
Importance of medicinal plants, available components and their application in different diseases.

Mechanism of absorption of water, active and passive absorption, external factors affecting absorption, conduction and translocation.
Transpiration, guttation, type, significance, mechanism of opening and closing of stomata, factors affecting transpiration.
Source, the general function of micro and macro elements in plant growth and development, deficiency symptom.
Mechanism of mineral salt absorption and translocation.

General account and modern concept, pigments in prokaryotes and eucaryotes, light and chemical reactions, photophosphorylation, factors affecting photosynthesis, pathways of carbon-di-oxide reduction in C3, C4 and CAM plants, source and sink relationship, significance.
Respiration of plant and microbes, types, respiratory substances, different pathways, fermentation, efficiency of respiration, production of high energy compound and ATP, photorespiration.

Definition, basic concepts of growth and development, measurement, vegetative and reproductive growth, phages of growth, factors affecting growth and development, principle and problem of cell differentiation and morphogenesis in plants, senescence, type and causes of senescence.

Definition, occurrence, classification, nature and effect of growth regulating chemicals on plant growth and development with special emphasis on auxin, gibbrellin, cytokinin/ kinin, abscisic acid, ethylene, and plant growth retardants.
Mechanism of flowering, florigen and its role in flowering, light image, and flowering.
Definition, types, importance, etc.
Light sensing by plants, photomorphogenesis, phytochrome and blue light photoreceptors, the effect of UV light on the biological system, the significance of biological clocks.

cos: Describe the diversity of plant form and function, expression and inheritance of traits
Recognize the economic importance of cereals, vegetables, fruits, and medicinal plants.
Communicate the importance of plant science in addressing significant challenges facing society, including examples of how plant scientists have “solved” such problems.
Development of personal skills to conduct plant science and plant physiological research
Contributing to develop plant based pharmaceuticals and industry

PLS 0511 1126.rationale: This course consists of a series of laboratory exercises to familiarize students with main concepts and techniques of plant sciences and plant physiology.
objectives: To acquaint students with the basic tools used in the research of plant sciences

To learn some aspects of plant physiology like- diffusion, osmosis, osmotic pressure, transpiration, photo-periodisom by hands-on experience and to become acquainted with techniques and methods often used in those areas of plant physiology.

contents.t: Identification of laboratory specimen and detailed plant cell structure, organelles, etc.
Identification of plant body, flower, and fruit plants, etc.
Details morphology study of Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, Tobacco, Lentil, Nut, Cotton, Jute, etc.
Identification of economic and medicinal plants, their essential parts, isolated compounds role, etc.

Experiments on Transpiration, guttation.

Seed germination and seed viability test.

Interpret the basic mechanism of different physiological process of plants.
Explain the concept of plants growth, development and their interaction with environment.

MCB 0511 1127.rationale: The course will provide basic knowledge on microorganisms, but will emphasize bacteria. This course will help students to be familiar with the fundamental concepts and basic skills utilized in microbiology to enable them to expand their knowledge of the microbial world.
objectives: Help students conceptualize the basic microbiological principles
To provide the basic knowledge about the members of microbial world and their roles in Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (GEB)
Acquaint students with the microscopy of different types of microbes
To facilitate necessary knowledge about taxonomy, sterilization, disinfection, growth, and culture methodologies of microorganisms

contents.t: Definition of microorganism and microbiology; Place of microorganisms in the living world; A brief history of the development of microbiology – early observation of microorganisms, the debate over spontaneous generation, the germ theory of disease, vaccination and discovery of antibiotics; Modern developments in microbiology; Scope of microbiology.

Salient features of major types of microorganisms: bacteria, archaebacteria, rickettsia, mycoplasma, actinomycetes, fungi, algae, protozoa, virus, viroids, prions; Classification based on temperature, pH, oxygen, salinity, nutrients, and pressure.
Morphology; Structure - Capsule, flagella, pili, cell-wall, cytoplasmic membrane, inclusion bodies, ribosome, pigments, and endospore; Classification; Multiplication; Economic importance.
Culture medium – simple, defined, complex, selective, differential and enrichment media; Batch and continuous culture; Anaerobic culture methods; Culture preservation and management.
Nutritional and physical requirements for growth; Growth equation; growth curve; Measurement of growth.
Sterilization- Principles of sterilization, methods of sterilization; Effect of anti microbial agents.

Ecology and ecosystem; Biotic and abiotic factors; Microorganisms in the soil, air, and water; Microbial interaction – neutralism, synergism, mutualism, commensalism, antagonism, parasitism, and predation.

contents.h: Isolation and identification methods of Microorganisms
contents.t: Isolation of microorganisms; Morphological, cultural, biochemical, serological and molecular techniques for the identification of microorganisms.

cos: Recognize the importance of microorganisms in GEB.
Recognize the diversity of microorganisms and microbial communities.
Apply knowledge to microscopic studies and interpret the structural similarities and differences among prokaryotic and eukaryotic microorganisms.
Identify the structure-function relationships of bacterial cells and viruses.
Design culture media and methods for bacterial growth, and identify techniques for controlling and routine maintenance of microorganisms safely and effectively.

objectives: Acquaint students with the basic tools used in microbial techniques
To facilitate necessary knowledge about aseptic, sterilization and bacterial cultural techniques
Make the students understand the isolation and identification procedures for bacteria and fungi
Helping the students to develop ability in analysis of antimicrobial activity of pathogenic bacteria and fungi

Identify the procedures for preparation of different culture media used in bacterial cultivation and characterization
Perform different staining techniques for bacteria
Utilize different techniques to measure bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility test
Identify and manage biohazards for humans, biodiversity and the environment

GEB 0512 1231.rationale: This course aims to provide an advanced and excellent understanding of the principles and topics of Biochemistry and their experimental basis by lecture-based classes, and to enable students to acquire a specialized knowledge to understand molecular biology, biotechnology and genetic engineering.
objectives: To teach the students about life and living things.
To provide information about biochemically important aspects of the chemistry of proteins, carbohydrates, nucleic acids and lipids, using appropriate examples.
To give emphasis on understanding the structural principles that govern reactivity/physical properties of biomolecules.
Understand the importance of biomolecules for living beings.

contents.t: Biochemistry, its definition, and scopes, the relation between biochemistry with biology, medicine and agriculture, the concept of life and living processes, the identifying characteristics of a living matter. Biomolecules-
Physical and chemical properties of water, pH, buffer, Henderson Heschel equation.

Occurrence, nomenclature, biological importance, chemical characteristics, and classification of carbohydrates. Monosaccharides and disaccharides: structure, properties, characteristic tests, amino sugars, and glycosides. Polysaccharides: occurrence, compositions, structure and properties of starch, glycogen, cellulose, other polysaccharides of biological interest, their chemical tests and biological importance, analysis of carbohydrates.
Definition, classification and biological importance.

Amino acids: definition, source, classification and structure of naturally occurring amino acids and their physical, chemical and optical properties, essential and non- essential amino acids, concept of residue, peptide bonds, oligopeptide and polypeptide, identification of N-terminal and C-terminal residue of a peptide, synthesis of peptides. Proteins: definition, classification, and biological importance.

General structure of nucleosides and nucleotides, the chemistry of DNA, base pair rule, double helical structure, the chemistry of RNA, types, and functions of RNA, physiochemical properties, denaturation and renaturation of nucleic acids.
Definition, classification, their functions and importance in Biochemistry.

cos: Get insight the life and its components, features of life including differentiation between living and non-living things etc.
Recognize the structure/conformational freedom of biomolecules, e.g., carbohydrates, proteins, DNA/RNA lipids etc.
Realize the important role and mode of hormonal action.
Discover the fundamentals of different diseases that are caused by the deficiency of vitamins

GEB 0512 1233.rationale: This core course presents an overview of the structure and function of cell and its organelles. This course mainly focused broad spectrum of eukaryotic cell biology including membrane structure and composition, structure of cytoskeleton, cellular transport and trafficking, cell division, cytogenetics, and impact of defective cellular process in human diseases.
objectives: To know structure and composition of a cell and its organelles
To understand cell division and different other cellular processes
To familiar with different cellular deregulation and its impact
To get insights of cytogenetics and cause of different genetic diseases

contents.t: Historical background of the cell, cell discovery, and organelles. Definition and modern concept of a cell, protoplasm theory. Cell types and structure: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells. The typical structure of the eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell and their functions.

Major cellular organelles, composition, structure and function. Cell wall membrane, plasma membrane, nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, mitochondria, chloroplast, ribosome, lysosome, cytoskeletal structure.
Structure and function of the nucleus, types of chromosome, morphology, and chemistry of chromosome, the function of chromosome

Definition and purpose of cytogenetics, different parts of a chromosome, types of chromosome, concept and importance of karyotyping, why metaphase chromosomes are used for karyotyping, general steps of karyotyping, banding patterns of chromosomes, types of banding, Idiogram, use of karyotyping in chromosomal disorders detection.

Deletion- definition, types, phenotypic effect, genetic effect, Duplication- definition, types, Phenotypic effect, Bridge-breakage-fusion Cycle, Meiosis, and breeding behavior. Inversion, types, cytology, Identification of parasitic inversion. Translocation; Definition, types, origin, meiotic behavior,
Euploidy, Aneuploidy, polyploidy, Autopolyploidy and Allopolyploidy.
Types of cell division, steps of mitosis and meiosis, the difference between the two processes, Abnormalities in mitosis and meiosis, causes and significance. Spermatogenesis and Oogenesis
Cell visualization, culture, fractionation and counting techniques.

cos: Describe the fundamental and modern concept of cell biology
Realize structure and function of cell and its organelles
Recognize cytoskeleton, cellular transport and trafficking, and cell movement
Know events of cell divisions and impacts of its disregulations
Analyze impact of structural and numerical anomalies of chromosome
refs: De Robertis, E.D.P., and Derobertis. Jr. E.M.F.(1989).Cell and Molecular Biology. 8th Edition, Info. Med. Ltd. Hong Kong.
Smith and Wood (1996).Cell Biology 2nd edition. Chapman and Hall Co. Ltd. UK.
Gupta P.K., Cytogenetics.

GEB 0512 1234.rationale: This course is designed to provide hands on knowledge about the structure and function of cell and cellular organelles.
objectives: To know structure and composition of animal and plant cell
To understand different stages of cell division
To handle cases with chromosomal anomalies
To get insights of cytogenetics and cause of different genetic diseases

Study of meiosis in the pollen mother cells of onion/maize.
Effect of colchicine treatment on onion/garlic root tip chromosomes.
Effect of gamma - ray irradiation on onion/garlic root tip chromosomes.
Study of Giant chromosomes of 3rd instar larvae of Drosophila melangaster .
Study of chromosomal aberrations in the Chromosomes of Musca domestica.
Effect of different herbicides on salivary gland chromosome in Musca domestica.
Effect of different plant extracts on oocyte chromosome salivary gland chromosome in Musca domestica.

cos: Recognize the sub-cellular structures, cell types, tissues, and organs
Obtain knowledge how to relate microscopic morphology to cell/tissue/organ function
Use of histological knowledge and techniques used in modern cell biology
Get insight the molecular mechanism of chromosomal aberrations

Gupta P.K., Cytogenetics

GEB 0512 1235.rationale: The course will provide basic knowledge of genetics and the science of heredity, from its basic principles to the most recent advances in the field.
objectives: To learn the basic principles of genetics from Mendel and his works, will know how sex is determined in plants and animals.
Describe various types of genetic crosses and indicate when/why they would be used by a geneticist.

To explain more complex modes of inheritance and compare the effects of linkage and crossing over on genetic outcomes and assess data. To define and identify the various types of mutations those occur at the DNA and protein levels.

contents.t: Historical background of genetics. The modern concept of genetics, Scope and branches, Application and Importance of genetics in human society. Some important genetical terms. Heredity and variation.

The Life history of Mendel. Discovery of Mendel works. The experiment of Mendel work. Mendel's law of segregation and independent assortment. The exception of Mendelism: Modification of Mendelian ratios. Lack of dominance, co-dominance, over dominance, Epistasis, interaction, lethal gene.

Multiple allelism, Characteristic features, inheritance pattern of a multiple of rabbit coat color, pleiotropism human and plants. Blood groups inheritance in man and plasma protein polymorphism in man.

Linkage, crossing over, different kinds of linkage and crossing over and their significance, linkage groups. Factor affecting the strength of linkage, cytological demonstration of crossing over. Linkage maps of Drosophila, chromosome map.
Cytological and genetic basis of sex determination. Different mechanism of sex determination in plants, animals and its implication.
Definition, types of mutagen and mutation, characteristics, causes and effects of gene mutation and mechanism.
Extra nuclear inheritance in prokaryotes and Eukaryotes, Plasmid, Mitochondrial and Chloroplast DNA, Maternal inheritance.

cos: Describe genetic diversity of animal and plant and apply the principles of inheritance as formulated by Mendel.
Apply the principles of extensions to Mendelian inheritance, including multiple allelism, lethal alleles, gene interactions, and sex-linked transmission.
Describe normal chromosome number, structure, and behavior in human cells, and recognize the cause and effect of alterations in chromosome number and structure
Realize how to identify and classify mutations in DNA and explain deviations from fundamental genetics in eukaryotes
refs: Verma, P.S. and Agarwal, V.K 1985.: Genetics (6th edn) S. Chand and Co. Ltd. New Delhi.
Gardner, E.J., Simmons, M.J. andSnustad. D.P. 1991. : Genetics (18thed) John Wiley and Sons. New York.
Strickberger, M.W. 1968. : Genetics. McMillan, New York.

GEB 0512 1250.rationale: This course aims to ensure that the students are able to present or answer or demonstrate their knowledge in front of an examiner panel at the end of the each year which they have achieved from the theory or practical courses in the same year.
objectives: Evaluate the student’s capacity to present/demonstrate their achieved knowledge in course work
Assess the student’s ability to perform or answer in different environment or public places.

Evaluate the student’s skill in managing their answer in front of examiners panel.

contents.t: Based on the courses taught in First Year.

cos: Identify the depth of knowledge in the course-work.
Improve their capacity to present achieved knowledge.
Recognize how to manage/perform in an unknown environment.
Scale-up presentation capability to communicate or manage other persons.

ANS 0511 2121.rationale: This course is designed for detailed study of the physiological processes of all body systems of the human body and different economical important animals on an appropriate level (knowledge, comprehension, application and analysis). It also provides fundamental principles of physics and chemistry to the understanding of the body’s function and regulatory mechanisms.
objectives: To study about how the human and higher animal body works.
To understand the role of body systems and mechanisms in maintaining homeostasis and how the activities of organs are integrated for maximum efficiency.

Describe the fundamental mechanisms underlying normal function of cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems of the human body, commensurate with the requirements for a physician providing primary care to patients.
To train student to solve physiology and related common clinical problems by applying physiologic principles.

contents.t: Introduction, definition, branches of physiology, glossary and terminology related to physiology.

Definition and different composition of blood and plasma proteins, their structure, functions, development and fate. Blood coagulation mechanism, blood groups, lymphoid system. Structure and properties of cardiac muscle, generation and conduction of cardiac impulse. E.C.G, events of cardiac cycle and cardiac outputs, factor affecting heart rate, haemodynamics, blood pressure and its regulation, fetal circulation and maternal circulation.
Different parts of respiratory system, functions and pulmonary circulation, mechanisms of respiration. O2 and CO2 transport in the body, regulation of respiration- nervous and chemical.

Functions of kidney, renal circulation, Nitrogenous excretory substances of different animals. urine formation in mammals, birds, reptiles. Filtration, reabsorption of different components of tubular fluid, excretion, concentration of urine, concept of plasma clearance, acidification of urine.
Functions of digestive system, digestive enzymes, mechanisms of secretions of gastric juice, physiology of digestion and absorption of food (carbohydrates, proteins and fats).
Physiology of reproductive systems, puberty, estrous and menstrual cycle, physiology of gestation and milking.
Endocrine and exocrine glands of male and female, growth and sex hormones, structure, functions and mechanisms of regulation of hormones.

Classification of nervous system, structure and functions of neuron, synapse, neurotransmitter and transmission of nerve impulse, control of sensory and motor function. Organization of nervous system, cerebral cortex, brain stem, cerebellum and spinal cord. Physiology of Special Senses: Physiology of special sensory organs concern with vision, sound perception, taste, and smell and touch.

cos: Describe the physiological processes that regulate body functions and the regulation of an organ system from the molecular level to all the way to the whole animal level
Describe interactions between different organ systems (homeostasis)
Distinguish the anatomy of different physiological systems and their specific functions
Discover how changes in one system may impact a different system
Apply knowledge of a physiological mechanism to explaining how a whole animal physiological process occurs.
refs: Ganong, W. F., :Review of Medical Physiology.
Guyton, A. C. and Hall, J.E., :Textbook of Medical Physiology
Hafez, E.S.E: Reproduction In Farm Animals
Swenson, M.J. : Duke’s Physiology of Domestic Animals.

ANS 0511 2122.rationale: Animal and Human Physiology Lab is a course that will provide practical knowledge on body functions, general anatomy, and physiological processes of the animal and human body.
objectives: To recognize the anatomical body structures and organs and how these are combined into organ systems within the body.
To know about the basic knowledge of human and animal physiology and its implication for human welfare.
To learn the physiological processes associated with the body and how they interact and function.

GEB 0512 2123.rationale: This course will give an overview of different types of biofertilizers used in Bangladesh and worldwide and their production procedure and to introduce students to renewable energy resources availability, potential andthe portability as a substitute for conventional energy resources in future energy demand.
objectives: To teach the basic principles of biofertilizers and different scientific methods of biofertilizer production along with their applications.
To develop the outstanding environmental safety concern about chemical-based fertilizers and importance of establishing biofertilizer in national paradigm.
To make student aware of the recent demand of renewable energy and what role they can play as a biotechnologist to meet the energy demand in perspective of Bangladesh.

contents.t: Definition, types of biofertilizer,, importance of biofertilizer for different crops, mass cultivation, Soil fertility, Nitrogen Cycle and Nitrogen Fixation: Sources of nitrogen, N2-cycle, forms of soil nitrogen, amount of nitrogen-fixed. Factors affecting nitrogen fixation. Methods discharge of electricity, activity of symbionts, activity of free fixers, manufacture of synthetic nitrogen. Interactions of O2 with N2- fixation; supplies of electrons; energy requirement for N2 fixation. Mechanism of penetration of Rhizobium into roots, signal exchange before cell infection, interaction at the root hair surface infection, infection thread development and nodulation; function of the nodule; measurement of N2 fixation. Factors affecting nodule development. Nitrogenase: Discovery, nature and mode of action and mechanism of nitrogen-fixation.

Nif+ and Nif- ; genetics of Nif in Klebsiella pneumoniae; structure and regulation of Nif genes in K. penumoniae, Rhizobium and Anabeana. Isolation, Identification and Classification of Microorganisms used as Biofertilizers: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillium, Frankia and Mycorrhizae. Production of Biofertilizers: a) Rhizobium: Mass-production, inoculants, quality control, methods of inoculation and agronomic improtance. b) Azotobacter: Physiology and fuction, crop response. c) Azospirillium: Physiology and function, Inoculant, crop response. d) Frankia: Infection and nodule development. e) Mycorrhizae: Types, physiology and function, inoculum production and inoculation techniques. Blue Green Algae (BGA): Nitrogen transformations in a low land rice ecosystem; heterocysts-modes of nitrogen fixation in BGA, isolation of BGA, agroclimatic variations; algalization-mass cultivation; multiplication of BGA in the field and effect of inoculation on the yield of rice, pay off from BGA inoculant. General Discussion on- Azolla, green manure, algae and soil reclamation, organic matter composting and phosphate solubilizing microorganisms, benefits from biofertilizers. Renewable Energy: Introduction: Sources of energy, types of energy. Biomass: Sources of biomass, composition of biomass, terrestrial and aquatic biomass, formation of biomass. Solar Energy: Photosynthesis, solar energy as a fuel replacement, production of hydrocarbon from plants. Biomass as Fuel Energy: Methods of biomass for energy, different types of fuels, biomass fuel fields, Hydrolysis, municipal solid waste. Biomass Conversion: Non-biological process and biological process. Gaseous Fuel: Biogas and Hydrogen, Procedure for biogas making and its utility, production of Hydrogen from biomass. Liquid Fuel: Alcohol- ethanol production from biomass, future prospects of industrial alcohol bio diesel, bio butanol etc. Biomass and Environment: Environmental impacts and remedies, other important issues.

cos: Identify different types of biofertilizers available in the environments to provide nutritional supports naturally.
Develop different skills in order to produce biofertilizers for land and accumulate basic ideas about the scale up production for industry.
Apply the knowledge of molecular biology to develop genetically engineered microorganisms can be used as biofertilizer.
Develop methods for the commercialization of biofertilizers
Recognize most important renewable energy sources like solar energy, biomass energy, hydro power, wind power, different types of gaseous and liquid fuels.

GEB 0512 2124.rationale: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students to biofertilizer and renewable energy resources availability, potential and deportability as a substitute for future demand.
objectives: To provide the advanced knowledge about potential of using biofertilizer and renewable energy technologies as a complement and to the extent possible.
Learn how to apply the knowledge for accelerating renewable energy technology development in different sectors.

Nodulation experiments.
Biofertilizer preparation and seed treatment
Study on algalization technique.
Study on Azolla spp. mass cultivation of Rhizobium etc.
Organic matter composting processes.

Outline the isolation and characterization of a microorganism
Describe algalization technique
Outline the process of biofertilizer preparation
Explain the composting processes in details

GEB 0512 2125.rationale: This course is designed to introduce different aspects of microbial genetics. It starts with basic mechanisms of microbial and phage genetics which extends to their particular applications.
objectives: To familiarize with fundamental organization and processes of microbial genome, plasmids and gene transfer.
To introduce phage genetics and applied microbial genetics in practice.

contents.t: The evolution of microbial genetics, early concepts of bacterial variation; adaptation, mutation and selection; dominance and recessiveness of characters, difference with eukaryotic genetics.

General aspects of prokaryotic gene regulation; regulation of the metabolism of lactose-the LAC operon; catabolite repression; regulation of the biosynthesis of tryptophan-the TRP operon; two-component regulatory system. Genetics of Bacteria: Bacterial conjugation, transformation, transduction, chromosomal transfer; interrupted mating experiments. Plasmids: Types, transfer, replication, detection and construction of recombinant plasmid vectors. Genetics of Yeast and Fungi: Mating type genetics of yeast, yeast plasmid, mitochondrial inheritance of yeast, Special study of Yeast genetics, Eukaryotic models: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe as model in understanding eukaryotic gene expression and cellular biology. PCR based gene tagging and deletion, transformation and homologous recombination in S. pombe. Genetics of Viruses: Genetics of bacteriophage; cosmid and phagemid vectors. Microbial model organisms: Prokaryotic model : E. coli as model in understanding prokaryotic gene regulation, cell biology. Eukaryotic models: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe as model in understanding eukaryotic gene expression and cellular biology. PCR based gene tagging and deletion, transformation and homologous recombination in S. pombe.

cos: Account the basic aspects of microbial genome, plasmids, and gene transfer processes e.g. conjugation, transduction and transformation.
Realize genetic mapping of microorganisms as well as recognize the role of transposable elements.
Display the regulation processes of prokaryotic gene expression and recognize the extrachromosomal inheritance pattern in microorganisms
Link microbial genetics with industrial application as well as environment
refs: Avers, C. J. (1990). Genetics. Freeman and co. NY.

GEB 0512 2127.rationale: This course provides basic knowledge and information on enzymology. It will emphasize on enzyme- based catalytic models, enzyme kinetics and factor affecting enzyme catalysis rate and enzyme inhibition. Students will be introduced theoretically with mechanisms based on which therapeutic drugs are used on enzyme mediated metabolic pathways.
objectives: Give basic concepts of enzymes and inhibitors.
Explain the function and action of enzymes.
Illustrate enzyme regulation and inhibition and their application in industries like drug, agriculture etc.

contents.t: Brief history, enzymes as biological catalysts, classification, nomenclature, enzyme assay, specific activity, enzyme activity units.

contents.h: Factors Affecting the Rate of Enzymatic Reactions
contents.t: substrate concentration, enzyme concentration, pH, temperature, coenzyme and cofactor.

Monosubstrate reactions, Michaelis-Menten equation and its linear transformations, Km, Vmax: definition, determination and significance. Double reciprocal plot or Lineweaver-Burk equation, kinetics of enzymatic reactions having two or more substrates.
Reversible inhibition, competitive, non-competitive and uncompetitive inhibition. Irreversible inhibition, specific examples.
absolute specificity, broad specificity, intermediate specificity, and stereospecificity.
Allosteric enzymes, cooperativity special characteristics, Monod and Koshland models, covalent modification of enzymes, specific examples (Ribonuclease, ATPase, phosphorylase, and dehydrogenase).
Chymotrypsin, Ribonuclease A, Lysozyme etc.

cos: Explain the concept of using protein and enzymes for industrial and therapeutic purposes.
Outline the molecular techniques to increase enzymes and proteins efficiency.
Describe enzyme kinetics, regulation and inhibition.
Modify and design existing proteins and enzymes for increasing their efficiency for various applications.
Apply the knowledge of particular enzymes working mechanism in various industrial processes and agriculture sector

GEB 0512 2129.rationale: This course intends to provide a substantial introduction to modern cellular and molecular biology and understand the molecular mechanisms of life.
objectives: To provide concrete knowledge on the central dogma of molecular biology.
To give a comprehensive idea to the students about the basic knowledge of DNA, genomes, genes, transcription, RNAs, translation, gene mutation, gene expression and gene regulation.
To understand fundamental knowledge of molecular and cellular processes.
To familiarize the students with the experimental approaches used in molecular biology.

contents.t: Chemistry of nucleic acids, structure, physico-chemical properties, molecular weight determination of nucleic acids, structure and physico-chemical properties of DNA and RNA, hybridisation kinetics, homoduplex, different configuration of cruciform structure. Central dogma of Molecular Biology- DNA Replication: Mode of replication, types of replication, DNA synthesis, mechanism and control of DNA replication, inhibitors of replication, DNA polymerase and other replication proteins. Transcription: RNA polymerase, promoter, enhancers and terminators, mechanism of transcription, reverse transcriptase, regulation of transcription, operon model and RNA spicing, genetic codes, its characteristics, specificity. Pre mRNA processing in Eucaryotes: Mechanisms Capping, Splicing and Poly adenylation in Eucaryotes. Translation: Ribosome structure, initiation, elongation and termination of protein synthesis, compare of protein synthesis in eukaryotes and prokaryotes, inhibitors of protein synthesis, post-translational modification. Mutation and genome stability: Molecular basis of mutation, in vitro mutagenesis, and site directed mutagenesis, repair mechanism in mutation. DNA repair system and genome stability. Regulation of Gene Expression: Gene from different kinds of RNA, RNA polymerase, positive and negative control of gene expression, gene expression of somatic cell hybrids. RNA degradation by nonsense mediated mRNA decay (NMD). Molecular Biology of Organelle: Genomes of the mitochondria and plasmid, interaction with nucleus, duel control of its synthesis. Mobile genetic elements : Mobile genetic elements in eukaryotes – relevant to plants, studies in maize, transposable elements in viruses, funi and other animals.

cos: Exhibit a theoretical knowledge based on genetics, cell and molecular biology. CO2 Demonstrate the knowledge of common and advanced laboratory practices in cell and molecular biology
Engage in review of scientific literature in the areas of molecular biology
Apply the knowledge of molecular biology.

GEB 0512 2131.rationale: This course will serve as a general introduction to the principles of plant breeding, information pertaining to modification and improvement of a wide range of crops, including both agronomic and horticultural crop species important in temperate and tropical areas.
objectives: To familiarize students in applying genetic techniques, statistical methods, breeding principles and methods to efficiently create and advance populations of plants from which there is a high probability of selecting superior cultivars or hybrids.

To provide knowledge of pollination, fertilization, and reproduction of plants and selection parameter, heterosis, heritability, double haploid, fertility gene manipulation and genetic gain concept for plant improvement.

contents.t: Definition, history, scope and objectives of plant breeding. Genetic basis of plant breeding. Contribution of national research institutes for the development of improved varieties of important crops.
Definition and classification of germplasm, gene pool concept, genetic erosion.

Definition, cause, Classification on the basis of the interaction between Pollen grain and pistil, Heteromorphic and Homomorphic system of self-incompatibility, Mechanism, elimination and temporary suppression of self-incompatibility.
Definition, ideal features of Apomictic system, classification, genetics of Apomixis, development of apomictic lines, application of Apomixis, advantage and problems in utilization of Apomixis.

Definition, classifications, phenotypic expression, Genetic Male sterity, molecular mechanism of ms action. Types of genetic male sterility, TGMS and PGMS lines, Transgenic genetic male sterility and their utilization in plant breeding.

Definition, objectives, prerequisites, advantages and disadvantages of hybridization. Selfing and crossing techniques, difficulties and precaution, rising of the F1 generation, techniques in field traits.

Heterosis; Types, scope, genetic, physiological and biochemical basis, use of heterosis in plant breeding. Heritability; Types, scope, genetic, physiological and biochemical basis, use of heritability in plant breeding. Inbreeding depression; Genetic effects of inbreeding depression (in plant, animals, human and fishes) practical application of inbreeding, genetical basis of inbreeding depression.

Self-pollinated crop; Mass selection, pure line selection, pedigree method, backcross methods and bulk method of selection and single seed discent method. Cross pollinated crop; Variety concept, mass selection, recurrent selection, ear to row selection, inbreed lines and evaluation of inbreed lines (general combining ability and specific combining ability), hybrid and synthetic varietydevelopment process and consequences.

contents.h: Release and Evaluation of New Varieties
contents.t: New crop varieties release and evaluation systems, Nucleus, Breeder, Foundation and Certified seeds, Role of NSB and SCA in seed development sector, Distribution of improved seeds from laboratory to farmers.

cos: Explain the principles and methods of plant breeding
Design conservation and management practices of plant genetic resources
Conduct and analyze a selection experiment
Identify the regulations surrounding plant breeding, seed production and variety development and bio-safety issues
Critically analyze journal articles related to plant breeding methods and approaches

objectives: To provide practical knowledge about ways of propagation of basic crops with regards to their modes of reproduction.
To familiarize students with the up-to-date methods and techniques applicable for development of various types of crop varieties and cultivars.

contents.t: Floral biology, pollination system and crossing techniques in crop plants, such as rice, wheat maize, tomato, beans, peas, groundnut, mustard and jute.
Demonstration of field experiments:
Demonstration of parental, hybrid and segregating populations and data collection.
Demonstration of breeding research activities in the GPB experimental farm.

Data analysis for variety testing and other experiments, using a RCB design-anova, test of significance and mean separation.
Plant characters’ association –correlation and regression analysis.
Estimation of heterosis, heritability and no. of genes controlling quantitative characters.

cos: Outline hybridization procedure of different crop plants
Design and execute breeding schemes
Plan, analyze and interpret field experimental data
Assess different plant breeding activities in research institutions

GEB 0512 2231.rationale: The course is designed to develop student’s knowledge and understanding of biochemical and molecular studies into metabolic pathways and processes occurring in living cells with a focus on human metabolism in health and disease.
objectives: To familiarize students about the basic knowledge of the biochemical conversions and molecular pathways of metabolism.
To make students understand the metabolic fates (synthesis/ degradation/ modification) of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins in monogastric and ruminant species.
To facilitate the necessary knowledge on the central mechanisms of molecular regulation and control in normal metabolism.
To acquire the theoretical understanding of some important metabolic disorders that caused by aberrant metabolic pathways.

contents.t: General aspects of metabolism and experimental approaches to the study of metabolism, metabolic and energy transfer pathways, basic concept of the control of metabolism.

Glycolysis (the glycolysis pathway, aerobic and anaerobic fate, regulation of glycolytic pathway, physiological importance of aerobic and anaerobic glycolysis). Tricarboxylic acid cycle and its regulation. Pentose phosphate pathway, glyoxalate pathway and their regulation.

Glycogenolysis, glycogenesis, and control of glycogen metabolism. Biosynthesis of carbohydrate: Gluconeogenesis, and its regulation, biosynthesis of dioligo and polysaccharides, glycoproteins, proteoglycan, sugar interconversions

Degradation of triglycerides and phospholipids, oxidation of fatty acids, propionate metabolism, ketone bodies (formation and utilization), utilization of fatty acids for energy production, oxidation and functional role of polyunsaturated fatty acids.
Outline of metabolism of amino acids decarboxylation, oxidative deamination, transamination, urea cycle and toxicity of ammonia.
One carbon metabolism or biosynthesis of fatty acids (saturated and unsaturated), cholesterol, B-carotene, triglycerides, steroid hormones, prostaglandins, prostacyclin, thromboxane, phospholipids.

cos: Recognize, Relate and outline the carbohydrates, proteins, and fats degrading as well as synthesis pathways and their ultimate outcomes.
Explain the dynamic diversity of the metabolic regulation, and how this is specifically achieved in different cells.
Evaluate the usefulness of these biochemical processes, and argue the harmful biochemical substances for the body and their metabolic fates.
Design an experiment to detect metabolic disorders.

GEB 0512 2233.rationale: Biotechnology is becoming increasingly important to food. Biotechnology has been used in food production for thousands of years (e.g. brewing, yoghurt, pickling, etc). The new Biotechnology has a high potential in food production and processing. This course will cover the applications of new biotechnology in food production or processing.
objectives: To understand a broad grounding in concepts, techniques and issues involved in food, food products and their processing
To introduced with food spoilage and their preservation
To furnish a student with knowledge and understanding of the basic biological and chemical processes of living cells and enzymes and how these are harnessed into industrial processes.

contents.t: Microorganisms (molds, yeasts, bacteria) important in food biotechnology, major biotech food products.

contents.t: Composition and food value of milk. Adulteration of milk. Pasteurisation of milk. Definition, composition and manufacture of Butter and butter products. Definition, classification, manufacturing and processing of different types of domestic and foreign cheese. Composition and manufacturing process of condensed and powder milk.

contents.h: Biotechnology in Fermented Dairy Products and Dairy Based Products

Preparation of squash from fruit, juice, non alcoholic fruit drinks, sour kraut, pickles, jam, jellies, and marmalades. Enzyme treatments and preservation of fruit products,

contents.h: General Principles of Fish and Meat Preservation
contents.t: General Principles of food preservation with special emphasis on fish and meat. Proximate composition and nutritive value of fish and meat.

contents.h: Freshness test of fish and Meat
contents.t: Organoleptic, microbial and chemical test. Post mortem changes of fish and animals and its importance in fish and meat processing.

Chilling of fish and meat with ice and preservative ice. Methods of freezing. Factors affecting the quality during chilling and freezing. Preservation by irradiation, effect of irradiation on the keeping quality.
Basic mechanism of fish and meat drying. Country method of meat drying. Different methods of drying/ dehydration of fish and other aquatic animals. Quality aspects of dried fish and meat.
Smoking as preservation and processing method of fish and meat.
Types of salting, technological aspects of salting, salting process and characteristic features of salting with special emphasis on Hilsa fish processing.
Principles of canning, preparation of raw material, canning operation, types of can materials, examination of can, prospect of canned food industry in Bangladesh.
Shidol, fish pest, fermented squid gut etc.
Surimi: Surimi as a special fish product, methods of surimi preparation, factors affecting surimi preparation. Minced fish, fish meal, fish silage, FPC, FPI, fish oil etc.
Food additives, packaging of food, storage, transportation, merchandising of various products with added value, food spoilage and food regulation, quality control of food processing.

cos: Analyze the positive role and benefits of microorganisms and enzymes in food production, processing and preservation.
Recognize basic biological and chemical processes of living cells, enzymes and microbial nutrition in relation to fermentation processes
Realize principles of inoculum/starter culture development for industrial fermentations, technologies used for substrate preparation and recovery and purification of fermentation products
Explain the flowchart unit operations in the processing and production a number of fermented products such as wine, beer, cheese, yoghurt and others
Describe effluent treatment and conversion of food and agricultural wastes

Make the students understand the biotechnological aspects of food processing of vegetable and animal origin.

GEB 0512 2235.rationale: The overall aim of the module is to enable students to understand the physiology of reproduction and the underlying principles and application of the methods used to artificially control reproduction and achieve genetic improvement. The course is designed to provide knowledge for the optimal use of genetic and genomic resources in animal production and the optimal approaches to changing those genetic resources in livestock.
objectives: Student will get basic understanding of the various aspects of reproduction in animal and understand the fundamental knowledge of oogenesis, fertilization, cleavage, gastrulation, and organogenesis in vertebrate species.
To apply advanced scientific, technological knowledge and skills of animal breeding in designing and managing breeding improvement of economical animal species.
To provide knowledge of genetic diversity, phenotypic variations and different population parameter.

contents.t: Definition and Scope of animal reproduction, relationship of reproduction with genetics, breeding and as well as biotechnology, types of reproduction in various species of animals, adaptive mechanisms of individuals with respect to reproductive ability, factors responsible for reproduction, fundamental characteristics of reproduction, present status and future outlook of animal reproduction.
Male and female reproductive system of economically important animals (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig and poultry).

Hormone and receptors related to animal reproduction, classification, properties function and mode of action of reproductive hormones, endocrine regulation system governing male and female reproduction, hormone assay, hormone like substances- growth factor and prostaglandins. Relationship between Genetics and endocrinology, endocrine and nervous system. Use of synthetic and placental hormone. Transport and survival of gametes and embryos in vivo.

Primordial germ cells, life history of the germ cells, oogenesis, biochemical aspects of oogenesis, ovulation, follicular atresia, the structure of the egg, spermatogenesis, sperm transport in the male and female genital tract, egg ‘pick-up’, movement of egg along the fallopian tube.

Puberty, modern concept of the attainment of puberty in male and female, practical application of puberty, estrous cycle, endocrine mechanism of sexual behavior, endocrine, physiologic and behavioral changes during estrous in different farm animals, breeding season and its effect on reproduction.

Fertilization, preparation of gametes, acrosome reaction, interaction of spermatozoa with the zona pellucida, gamete fusion, activation of the egg, cleavage, blastocyst formation, implantation, embryonic and fetal development, act of parturition.

contents.h: Reproductive Diseases and Failure, Reproductive Efficiency
contents.t: Common diseases of reproduction in both sexes of farm animals, reproductive disorders, recommended practices for improving fertility, Measures of reproductive efficiency, factors responsible for efficient reproduction, means of improving reproductive efficiency.

Need for animal products, concept of animal genetics, application of genetics in livestock and other economical animals. Concept of animal breeding. Its development and application, domestication of farm animals, development of breed association. Population, breeds and breed structure, design of breeding programs, breed evolution.

Diversity in animal agriculture, animal genetic resources (AnGR), status of genetic resources- extinct, critical, endangered, at risk, reasons for loss of genetic resources, management of genetic diversity, conservation and improvement of FAnGR and their wild relatives.

Gene and genotype frequencies, hardy-Weinberg law, factors changing genetic properties and gene frequency. Phenotypic Variation: Values and means, discrete and continuous variation, normal distribution, components of phenotypic and genetic variation, genotype- environment interaction, average effect of genes.

Heritability, repeatability and genetic correlation- definition, methods of estimation and their uses. Restricted maximum likelihood (REML) approach. Breeding value: Definition, estimation and uses, most probable producing ability (MPPA), transmitting ability, best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP), Quantitative trait loci (QTL).

Natural and artificial selection, selection objectives and selection criteria, mass selection, pedigree selection, family selection, progeny testing, sib testing, methods of selection for more than one traits. Selection for correlated traits. Single gene effect in animal breeding, Nucleus breeding system, accuracy of selection.Selection program for livestock improvement, prediction and estimation of selection response, selection limit.

Inbreeding, inbreeding depression, inbreeding coefficient, pure breed breeding, COse breeding, line breeding. Out crossing, crossbreeding, grading up, species hybridization, heterosis and its application. Selection for combining ability, formation of synthetic breeds, breed conservation.

Improvement goal, existing genetic resources, improvement policy, breeding policy and plans for improvement of farm livestock (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat), system of breeding for captive and pet animals, community based breeding program, nucleus breeding system (NBS), breeding for resistance to diseases and threshold traits.

cos: Find out the comparative structure and function of the male and female reproductive systems
Discuss the physiology of reproduction including endocrine, neuro endocrine and environmental factors.
Realize the basic principles of animal breeding and genetic constitution of animal population and related dynamics.
Evaluate economic traits, genetic parameters, their scale, methods of estimation and apply in deciding breeding strategy.

Demonstrate concepts of genetic evaluation, principles and procedures of animal selection for genetic improvement of animals and gathered knowledge in formulation of national breeding policy for improvement of farm animals to achieve specific goal.

Accumulate basic ideas about environmental pollutants generated by human activities
Make the students understand the modern trends in biotechnology for management, disposal and treatment of environmental pollutants
To provide the knowledge of biodeterioration, biodegration and bioremediation
Make the students understand the environmental pollution control by bioremediation using biochemical, microbial, molecular and phytoremediation approaches
To learn the basic idea about environmental wastes as the resources for new technology development

The water cycle, carbon cycle, nitrogen cycle, sulphur cycle, other biogeochemical cycles.

Definition pollution and their types, use of commercial blends of microorganisms and enzymes in pollution control, immobilized cells in pollution control, novel biotechnological approaches-use of genetic manipulation, enzymes and specialized bacteria.
Primary treatment, BOD, secondary treatment, disinfections and release, activated sludge, septic tanks, oxidation ponds, tertiary treatment.
sources of metals, metal bioavailability in the environment, mechanisms of microbial metal resistance and detoxification, effects of metal microbes interactions.
application of biosensors for the detection of environmental pollutants, isolation and enrichment of organisms capable of detoxifying environmental pollutants.

Persistence and biomagnification, recalcitrant industrial wastes, structure-recalcitrance relationship, factors affecting microorganisms to degrade xenobiotics.
Biodegradation and metabolism of pesticides, phenols, organic dyes, synthetic organic chemicals, petrochemicals.
Definition, approaches to bioremediation-environmental modification for bioremediation, microbial seeding and bioengineering approaches, DNA and RNA based methods.

To provide a basic concept on secondary metabolites production, cryopreservation of endangered plants, somaclonal and gametoclonal variation and their application in agriculture.

To develop the graduate capabilities of knowledge ability, comprehension and applications of plants in cell and tissue culture systems, and how cell and tissue culture contributes to global sustainability.

contents.t: Definition, types of culture and historical development, purposes of cell, tissue and organ culture, cellular totipotency, cell and tissue growth process, characteristics and measurement method, laboratory organization: Lab design, small and large equipment with their functions.

Lab, facilities, design, operation and management, aseptic technique for plant tissues, chemicals, instruments, glass wares, personal hygiene and laboratory safety management etc.. Laboratory Equipments and Sterilization: Major equipment, minor equipment’s, sterilization types, procedure etc. Culture Media and Plant growth regulators: Components, composition, functions of components, preparation of media. Solidification, media selection and maintenance of media. Micro propagation: Definition, direct and indirect method of different plant, factors of shoot and root multiplication. Protoplast Culture: Isolation, purification and culture of protoplast, development and application of somatic hybrids and cybrids. Production of disease free plants: Methods of virus elimination, virus indexing, eradication of pathogens other than virus, application and limitations. Somatic embryo genesis and suspension culture: Initiation of somatic embryo: callus and suspension culture, maintenance of callus and suspension culture, production and management of somatic embryo and its application, plant formation from somatic embryo. Culture of Anther/pollen, Ovule, Embryo, Endosperm and Their Uses: Rice, wheat, barley, maize, brinjal. Somaclonal Variation: Production and selection of somaclonal and gametoclonal variation, utilization of somaclone and gametoclone in agriculture, in vitro selection of disease resistant and stress tolerant plants. In-vitro Conservation of Plant Materials: methods and factors affecting in vitro conservation, maintenance of frozen culture. Industrial Application of Plant Tissue Culture: Secondary metabolites derived from plants and their uses. Techniques of selecting cell lines for high production of secondary products. Mass cultivation of plant cells, scale-up, isolation, immobilization and purification and limiting factors.

cos: Developthe basic concepts, types, importance and scope of plant tissue culture.
Distinguish different types of sterilization techniques to sterile different plant parts.
Analyze culture media components and growth regulators with their functions.
Apply tissue culture techniques to produce diseases free plant,micropropagation, protoplast culture, somaclonal variation.
Demonstrate recent methodologies used in plant tissue culture in industrial label with professionalintegrity.

GEB 0512 3122.rationale: Plant tissue culture is the science of growing plant cells, tissues or organs isolated from the mother plant, on artificial media. The purpose of this course is to give students a practical experience in techniques in plant tissue culture and crop development.
objectives: To familiarize students to the basic principles of plant tissue culture and its applications.
To provide hands-on experience of the most common of these techniques in labs and demonstrations of more advanced or uncommon techniques.
To conduct a procedure that is often used to propagate many plants of the same genetic background.
To apply the sterile techniques in different plant parts.

contents.t: Laboratory, personal safety, precaution and uses/operation of instruments available at the Lab.
Sterilization techniques of glassware, instruments, media and explants.
Techniques of media preparation and their stock solutions.
Selection and pre-treatment of different kinds of explants.
Detection of contamination of media and cultures.
Initiation of callus and regeneration.
Microscopic analysis of callus for cytodifferentiation.
Determination of appropriate stages of anther and pollen.
Protoplast Isolation and hybridization

contents.h: Exploration, selection, collection and growing of donor/mother plants
contents.t: Banana, orchids, strawberry, gerbera, rice, barley, maize etc.
Hardening techniques of plantlets.

cos: Apply aseptic techniques in plant tissue culture.
Calculate the volume of media preparation, stock solutions and working solutions.
Detect the contamination in media and cultures.
Explain protoplast isolation, culture, fusion and selection.
Demonstrate the hardening techniques of plantlets.

GEB 0512 3123.rationale: The course is designed to provide concepts and principles in Animal Cell culture and related technologies for cell culture and cell culture products for therapeutics and commercial interest.
objectives: To acquire the necessary theoretical skills on animal tissue culture perspective
To make students able to design, operate and manage a typical animal cell culture laboratory
To study and prepare the different composition of animal cell culture media
To provide detailed insights regarding the isolation of animal cells for in vitro studies, maintenance and manipulation of animal cells in vitro
To familiarize the students with basic cellular and molecular biology techniques involved in animal cell culture and their applications in a real-world research setting
To train students in handling large animal models for disease and development of therapies and treatments

contents.t: Definition, type and history and development, Importance of cell, tissue and organ culture.
Animal cell cultures new understanding, new developments. Animal cell culture technology in the 21st century.
Facilities, design, operation and management. Media: Components, composition, functions of components, preparation and media selection. Solidification and maintenance of media.
Essential, beneficial and useful additional equipments consumable items.
Types of microbial contamination, detection of microbial contamination, cross contamination, general safety, fire, radiation and biohazards.
Principles of sterilization of apparatus, reagents and media.

Substrate, gas phase, medium and temperature. The substrate: plastic and glass wares; tissue culture flasks, culture vessels. The gas phase: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, Medium and Supplements: physical properties, constituents of media, serum, serum-free media; selection of medium and serum, other supplements, incubation temperature.

contents.h: Isolation of Tissue and Primary Culture
contents.t: Culture of Mouse embryos and hen’s embryo cell.
epithelial cells, mesenchymal cells, neuroectodermal cells, hemopoietic cells. Culture of tumor tissue- general method, selective culture.
Organ culture, histotypic culture, filter wells.
Isolation of different types of animal tissue; fibroblast, liver, kidney, bone marrow and their uses, Physical methods of cell separation.
Routine observation and maintenance; cloning and selection of specific cell-types.

contents.h: Quantitation and Experiment with Animal Cell
contents.t: selection of cell line; experimental design; growth
cell counting, preparation of samples for enzyme assay and immune assay, preparation of samples for extraction of DNA and RNA.

cos: Explain the various components of cell and tissue culture media as well as establishment and optimization of media for particular purposes in different species and cell lines
Perform the common cell culture techniques, cytotoxicity and viability assays for toxicological and pharmacological studies
Design the experiment for development of primary established cell culture and characterize the various cell lines used in mammalian tissue culture in relation to their origins and uses.

Describe the criteria in consideration for scale up of cell culture as well as the appropriate cell model for a large-scale process involved in the production of human and animal viral vaccines and pharmaceutical proteins
