GEB 0512 3125.rationale: The course is designed to develop student’s knowledge and understanding of biochemical and molecular studies into metabolic pathways and processes occurring in living cells with a focus on human metabolism in health and disease.
objectives: Recognize the routes of proteins degradation, amino acid catabolism, and anabolism and association of some catabolic intermediates in disease formation in human body;
Detect the inborn errors of metabolism and apply the DNA technology to their study;
To provide detailed insights regarding the synthesis and importance of cyclic compounds in regular activities of a cell;
Acquire the fundamental of minerals metabolism and their roles in other complex biochemical compounds;
Enhancing the skills to recognize signs, symptoms and diseases caused by accumulation of heavy metals in living cells;
Help them to conceptualize the control and integration of metabolism

contents.t: Glucogenic and ketogenic amino acids, oxidative degradation of amino acids to specialized products, amino acid biosynthesis, regulation of amino acid metabolism, metabolism of folic acid, glutathione, methylmalonate, clinical correlations: phenylketonuria, alkaptonuria, folic acid deficiency. Nucleotide Metabolism: Overview metabolic functions of nucleotide, synthesis of purine and pyrimidine nucleotides, formation of deoxyribonucleotides, regulation of nucleotides biosynthesis. nucleotide degradation, biosynthesis of nucleotide coenzyme, nucleotide metabolizing enzymes as a function of cell

cycle and rate of cell division, antimetabolites of purine and pyrimidine nucleotide metabolism, Lesch- Nyhan syndrome, orotic aciduria. Heme Metabolism: Biosynthesis of porphyrin and hemoglobin, Regulation of porphyrin biosynthesis, Degradation of heme and RBC, Porphyrias, Billirubin biosynthesis, Jaundice. Mineral Metabolism: Ca, Fe, Cu, Mg, I, Mn, Zn- metabolism, calmodulin, hemosiderosis, deficiency of minerals, enzymes and metabolic reactions activated/regulated by Mn, Mg, Zn, Cu, Fe, Ca. Metal Toxicities: Toxicity of Hg, Pb, As, Cd.

cos: Identify metabolic end products and their inter-relationship with the TCA cycle.
Outline the hormonal regulation of metabolism and evaluate physiological and pathological situations (e.g. exercise, starvation, and diabetes).
Distinguish the various types of genetic mutation and inborn errors in metabolism, detection, and correction
Design experiments on diagnosing autosomal recessive disorders and possible treatment as well as recommend the food ingredients.

GEB 0512 3127.rationale: The Immunology course is designed to provide a foundation on the basic concepts and terminology of immunology.
objectives: To introduce the concepts of immune system, their integral components and the interplay among host immunity
To deliver the knowledge of fine coordination of immune components, problems associated with their absence of it and therapeutic approaches
To overview different immunopathological states and the techniques of deciphering immunological reactions

contents.t: Adaptive and innate immunity, cells of the immune system, soluble mediators of immunity, cytokine, antigens, haptens and carriers, immune responses, inflammation, opsonization, chemotaxis, phagocytosis, defense against intracellular and extracellular pathogens.

contents.h: Cells and Organs Involved in Immune Responses
contents.t: lymphocytes (T-cells, B cells, NK cells), mononuclear phagocytes, polymorphonuclear granulocytes, mast cells, platelets, antigen presenting cell, primary and secondary clonal expansion of lymphocytes.
Antibodies, classification, structure, function and mechanism of action; Cytokines and their functions.
Antigen-antibody binding, antibody affinity and avidity, antibody specificity and cross reactivity, antigen processing and presentation, T-cell antigen recognition.
Recognition of antigen by T cells, antigen presentation, the major histocompatibility complexes or MHC molecules, the role of cytokines and the regulation of immune responses.

Activities of complement proteins, activation of complement, classical pathway, regulation of classical pathway activation, alternative pathway, activation and amplification loop, their regulation, membrane attack complex, biological effects of complement.
Immunity to intracellular and extracellular bacteria, viral infections, and parasitic infections.

Immunodeficiency (AIDS), immunological tolerance, hypersensitivity, autoimmune disease, immune-neuroendocrine network, endocrine-immune modulation, neuro-immune modulation, neuroendocrine and immune effect of psychosocial stress, effect of psychosocial stress on infection, allergy, cancer, AIDS and autoimmunity, immune activity and psychopathology, immune function enhancement.

cos: Acquire a fundamental working knowledge of the basic principles of immunology
Interpret how these principles apply to the process of immune function
Develop the ability to solve problems in clinical immunology by making use of the available resources and communicating with colleagues

GEB 0512 3129.rationale: The course will provide comprehensive theoretical knowledge on molecular techniques used in the field of genetic engineering and biotechnology.
objectives: To help students conceptualize the basic principles of molecular techniques commonly used in biotechnology.
To provide the knowledge about the applications of different techniques used in molecular biology.
Acquaint students with the limitations, advantages and disadvantages, troubleshooting of common problems associated with different molecular techniques.
Having an appreciation and knowledge of how to deal with ethical issues relating to science.

contents.t: Principle of sedimentation, centrifuges and their use, density gradient centrifugation and ultracentrifuge.
Principle of chromatography; column, thin-layer and paper chromatography; adsorption, gas liquid, ion-exchange, exclusion, affinity and high performance liquid chromatography.

Principle; factors affecting electrophoresis; gel electrophoresis, determination of restriction fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis. SDS-PAGE; isoelectric focusing; isotechnophoresis and preperative electrophoresis.
Nature, detection and measurement of radioactivity; application of radioisotopes in the biological sciences; safety aspects of the use of radioisotopes.
Ultraviolet (UV), Infra-red (IR), Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), Electron spin resonance (ESR) and mass spectroscopy.

contents.h: DNA and RNA isolation and Purification
contents.t: DNA and RNA isolation and purification, quantification of nucleic acid by spectrophotometry, fractionation of genomic DNA, plasmid DNA, mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.
Southern, Northern and Western blot hybridization, restriction endonuclease digestion of plasmid DNA.
Basic principles, methods and applications of PCR, RT-PCR, Primer design-degenerated and gene specific primers, forward and reverse primers, factors considering in the construction of primers.
Different methods of DNA sequencing.

cos: Acquire basic knowledge behind all molecular techniques used in the field of genetic engineering and biotechnology.
Apply the principles and techniques of molecular biology which prepares students for further education and/or employment in teaching, basic research, or the health professions.
Design experiments and properly interpret experimental data in order to carry out independent and collaborative research projects.
Implement the knowledge to operate all the equipment regularly used in molecular biology with complete accuracy, safely and appropriately.
Demonstrate a commitment to professional integrity and ethical behavior consistent with the mission of the university and accepted standards of professional conduct.

GEB 0512 3130.rationale: This course will provide practical knowledge on molecular biology techniques which eventually help the students to get hands-on training to solve scientific problems faced in biomanufacturing, pharmaceutical and biotechnology laboratories.
objectives: To acquaint students with the basic tools used in molecular biology
To gain necessary knowledge about spectroscopic methods, electrophoretic techniques, chromatographic separations, isolation and identification of macromolecules.
Helping the students to develop ability in analyzing the experimental data statistically and interpreting correctly.
Preparing the students to develop Communication skills in presenting their research findings through effective oral and written presentations.

contents.t: Studies on centrifugation using bench top, refrigerated high speed centrifuge machine.
Studies on nucleic acid and protein separation using Agarose, Starch gel, and SDS-PAGE electrophoresis.
Studies on spectrophotometer for optical density measurement and nucleic acid quantification
Genomic DNA, plasmid DNA isolation from plant and animal cell and purification, quantification of nucleic acid by spectrophotometry
Studies on PCR, RT-PCR, Construction of primer.
Studies on AFLP, RFLP.
Studies on DNA sequencing.
Southern, Northern and Western Blotting apparatus.
Thin-layer and paper chromatography and high performance liquid chromatography etc.

cos: Recognize how to handle basic instruments used to carry out molecular biology research works with complete accuracy, safely and appropriately.

Demonstrate industry-standard knowledge and skills in cloning, genomic and plasmid DNA isolation, PCR, restriction digest, gel electrophoresis, chromatographic separation, protein purification and quantification.
Acquire the basics of experimental design, how to formulate a hypothesis, what controls to use, how to interpret experimental data.
Develop communication skills in presenting their research findings through effective oral and written presentations.
Develop strong commitment to professional integrity and consistent ethical behavior.
refs: A Biologist’s Guide to Principles and Techniques of Lab. Biochemistry, 3rd edition: K. Wilson and K. H. Goulding.
Lab. Skills in Biomolecular Sciences: Rob Reed, David Holmes, Jonathan.

GEB 0512 3131.rationale: The course will provide basic knowledge of viruses. It will emphasise host-virus interaction, phage therapy, virus replication and the relationship between virus and cancer. Students will be introduced theoretically to how cancer and viral cells survive in the human body escaping the immune system.
objectives: Demonstrate an understanding of basic virology principles
Understanding the importance of viruses from clinical perspective
Acquire in depth knowledge to fight against emerging viral diseaes

contents.t: Brief history, nomenclature and classification, virion structure.
Attachment, entry and uncoating, replication, assembly and maturation, and virus exit from host cells.
specific examples: Influenza, EBV, Hepatitis, HIV, Dengue and Tumour viruses.
factors affecting the development of cancer, relation of oncogenes and oncogenic viruses for development of cancer, use of retroviruses as a vector for gene therapy and genetic engineering.
Replication and gene expression of DNA and RNA viruses-TMV, adenovirus, hepadnavirus, poxvirus, orthomyxoviruses, reoviruses, retroviruses.
Multiplication of T-even bacteriophages (lytic & lysogeny cycle), bacteriophages λ, gene expression and assembly of bacteriophages.
Principles of Bacteriophage therapy, Bacteriophage derived proteins (endolysin, virion-associated lysin) as potential therapeutics.

contents.h: Immunity, Prevention and Treatment of Viral Diseases
contents.t: Interferon interference, induction and activation, antivirals and viral vaccines.
General characteristics, virulence properties.

cos: Describe virus classification and host-virus interaction.
Recognize how to cultivate, purify and detect the presence of viruses.
Demonstrate the replicative strategies of different classes of viruses.
Utilize antiviral drugs and bacteriophage-based therapy against drug-resistant pathogens.
Realize the pathogenicity and the host immune response to viruses.
refs: Brock, T.D. Biology of Microorganisms.
Fields. Fundamentals of Virology
Jawetz E. J. et al. Review of medical microbiology

GEB 0512 3132.rationale: The course is designed to provide hand-on training to the students specially on various immunological and serological techniques and assays.
objectives: To recognize antigen-antibody interactions
To interpret immune assay techniques viz. immunofluorescence, radioimmuno, complements and enzyme-linked assay.

contents.t: Antigen-Antibody Interactions, Precipitation reaction in Gels, Haemaglutination and haemaglutination fixation test, Complement fixation, Direct and Indirect Immunofluorescence, Radioimmunoassay, Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay, Immunoblotting and Immunoprecipitations, Isolation of pure antibodies, Assay for Complements, Assay for Complements, Isolation of Lymphocyte population, Effectors’ Cell Assay

cos: Interpret antigen antibody interaction and precipitation reaction in gel and to explain the procedure of haemagglutination fixation and complement fixation test
Perform various assay techniques such as Radioimmunoassay, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay and Effectors’ Cell Assay
Isolate pure antibodies and lymphocyte population

BPE 0512 3133.rationale: The course is designed to enable graduate to incorporate in-depth relevant knowledge in processes and techniques for using biological agents such as cells, enzymes or antibodies for the production of chemicals, food, biofuels and pharmaceuticals, and waste treatment.
objectives: To provide the students with the necessary insight of the fundamentals of bio-catalysis, fermentation and bioreactor design, for the production of high value bio-products.
Get insight the different engineering principles to address issues in bioprocesses.
To impart knowledge on various methods of microbial cell disruption.
To provide knowledge about process engineering principles like mass transfer, thermodynamics and kinetics applied to biological systems.
Identify limiting factors in a bioprocess and propose solutions to address biological and engineering problems.
To help the students understanding the processes and applications of bio-composting.

contents.t: Concepts of bioprocess engineering, importance and application of bioprocess engineering, development of bioprocess engineering.

Static fluid property, pressure and pressure gauge, management of fluid pressure, one dimensional flow, velocity profile and velocity gradients, viscosity and boundary layer, linear and turbulent flow.
Introduction, analysis of disruption, laboratory scale and large scale of disruption techniques.
Introduction, classification of agitation, scope and objectives of agitation, equipment, factor affecting of agitation, applications.
Conduction, convection, radiation, natural forced convection, overall heat transfers co- efficient, dimensionless numbers.
Heat transfer in evaporators, classification and application of evaporators in food, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics industries, multiple effects of Evaporators,
Introduction; composting processes; succession of microorganisms; applications.

cos: Define the basic bioprocess engineering concepts of growth and product formation
Evaluate the kinetics of different fermentation process
Describe bioprocesses at the industrial scale
Analyze the mass and heat transfer in biochemical process
Recognize the differences in bioreactor design depending on the bioproduct synthetized and required cell type (bacteria, yeast, algae and mammalian cells)

GEB 0512 3231.rationale: This course begins with overviewing cell signaling, the diverse mechanisms used by cells to communicate, the major classes of signaling molecules and the receptor types upon which they act. It then focuses on signaling pathways that depend on regulated proteolysis and TGF super-family. This course also focused how cell response to the environmental stresses.
objectives: To know basic mechanism of cellular communication
To understand importance of cell signaling both in eukaryotes and prokaryotes
To familiar with different signaling pathways
To understand cellular interaction with microenvironment
To analyze role of cellular signaling in disease patho-mechanism

contents.t: Definition, steps of cell signaling, importance of cell signaling, cell signaling in unicellular and multicellular organisms.
Autocrine, paracrine, endocrine, contact dependent, synaptic, intracellular signaling, extracellular signaling.
Intracellular signaling molecules, extracellular signaling molecules, types of extracellular signaling molecules, signling specificity, primary messengers, secondary messengers.

Intracellular receptors (homodimeric receptor and heterodimeric receptor), structure of intracellular receptor, intracellular molecular switches, cell surface receptors, structure of cell surface receptor, types of cell surface receptors (G-Protein-coupled receptors, Enzyme-linked receptors, Ligand gated ion channels).

contents.h: Signaling Through G-protein-linked Cell Surface Receptors
contents.t: cAMP and G protein signaling, role of cAMP-dependant protein kinase (PKA) in mediating effects of cAMP, Inositol phospholipids signaling pathway, Ca2+ as an intracellular messenger, role of Ca2+/calmodulin-dependantprotein kinases in mediating actions of Ca2+, desensitization of G-protein-linked receptors.

contents.h: Signaling Through Enzyme-linked Cell Surface Receptors
contents.t: Receptor tyrosine kinases, docking sits for proteins, Activation of Ras, Ras cycles between active and inactive states, signals from activated Ras to a cascade of protein kinases including MAP-kinases, PI 3-kinase/ protein kinase B signaling pathway, Insulin receptor acts through PI 3-kinase pathway, Cytokine receptors and the JAK-STAT pathway, Two component signaling pathway of bacterial chemotaxis. Signaling Pathways that Depends on Regulated Proteolysis: Activation of Notch receptor by cleavage, binding of Wnt proteins to Frizzled receptors, stressful and proinflammatory stimuli act through NF-kB dependant signaling pathway.

Definition, structure and function of TGFß, Brief description of TGFß super family, factors responsible for activation of TGFß signaling, synthesis, secretion and maturation of TGFß ligand, TGFß receptors, canonical and non-canonical TGFß signaling pathway, inhibition of TGFß signaling, cross talk of TGFß signaling, dual role (tumor inducer and supressor) of TGFß.
Definition, process of synthesis and structure of BMP, BMP receptors, BMP signaling mediators, BMP signaling pathway, inhibition of BMP signaling pathway

Cellular stress responses, heat shock response, heat shock signaling, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, unfolded protein response (UPR), UPR signaling, DNA damage response, hypoxia and normoxia signaling. cellular response by oxygen deprivation.

cos: Demonstrate thorough knowledge of the major classes of signaling molecules, their receptors and intracellular signaling pathways
Recognize how these principles can be applied to the process of cell signaling
Develop the ability to solve problems in pathways that depends on regulated proteolysis and environmental approaches of signal-induced responses
Identify the different type of cell mediated receptors
Acquire a fundamental working knowledge of the different environmental approaches for signal induced response

GEB 0512 3233.rationale: This course aims to guide students in the use of bioinformatics applications available for the use of the information derived from the different fields of omics to generate knowledge and make discoveries based on informed interpretation.
objectives: Help the students conceptualize basics of bioinformatics and understand the interdisciplinary nature of bioinformatics
Provide knowledge about DNA, RNA and protein sequences and structures and makethem familiar with a variety of currently available genomic and proteomic databases, storage and management
Give practical knowledge about protein and nucleic acid sequence analysis and make them understand how to compare and analyze biological sequences and how to interpret the results of their analyses
To facilitate necessary knowledge of the genomic variations and consequences of genomic variations in human
Discuss the theory and practice of computational methods used in evolutionary bioinformatics and demonstrate the various servers and basic programming tools available through the internet
Demonstrate how to construct phylogenetic trees from biological sequence information
Make students aware of the applications of bioinformatics in broad ranges of field

contents.t: Definition,fundamentals of bioinformatics,interdisciplinary nature of bioinformatics, basics concept of genomics and proteomics, scopes andimportance of bioinformatics.

Types of biological databases, structures of data and databases,DNA and protein sequence and structural databases, retrieval of biological data and sequences Profile and motifs data bases, domain searches of databases

contents.h: Protein and nucleic acid sequence analysis
contents.t: Concept of structural bioinformatics, Basic local Alignment Search tool (BLAST), BLASTprinciples and search strategies, BLAST statistics, pairwise sequence alignment and scoring matrices (PAM and BLOSUM), sequence alignment algorithms: global and local, multiple sequence alignment(MSA) and approaches, use of different BLAST, pairwise and multiple sequence alignmenttools

different types of variation, variation in the human genome, known examples of diseases causing variations and SNPs, consequences of genomic variations, different genomic variation databases and their uses
Concept molecular evolution, principles and goals of phylogeny and evolution, properties and typesof phylogenetic tree, stages of phylogenetic analysis, phylogentic tree construction methods
Applications of bioinformatics in agriculture and food, environment, medical, human health and diseases diagnosis etc.

cos: Describe the basic knowledge and development of different Omics technologies and explain the interdisciplinary nature of bioinformatics
Utilize different databases and the algorithms of different bioinformatics tools and servers
Utilize applications of bioinformatics in different fields and apply the knowledge of complex evolution and explain evolutionary concept with bioinformatics
Explore protein and nucleic acid data acquisition, analysis and interpretation

GEB 0512 3234.rationale: Introduce students to the current bioinformatics algorithms/concepts and their implementations as well as provide practical knowledge and demonstration to develop analytical skills.
objectives: This course is designed to introduce students to bioinformatics tools and analysis methods
Provide knowledge about DNA and protein sequences and 3D structures
To develop skills to perform similarity searching, pairwise and multiple sequence alignments
Give the basic understandingof molecular evolution andconstruction of phylogentic tree

GEB 0512 4237.rationale: The course focuses on the vast array of applications in animal biotechnology and genetic engineering. Lectures will cover embryo transfer in domestic animals, In vitro fertilization in ruminants, genetic manipulation, micromanipulation of farm animal embryos, cloning and techniques for genetic engineering. contents.t: Application of Biotechnology for animal production. Embryo Transfer Technology in Domestic Animals: Definition, history, advantages and applications of embryo transfer. Steps in embryo transfer technique: selection and management of donor and recipients; super ovulation; estrus synchronization; estrus detection; insemination of the donor; preparation of culture media; collection of embryos using surgical and non-surgical methods. Handling of embryos: identification of embryos; evaluation of embryos; cryopreservation of embryos; transfer of embryos limitations of embryo transfer techniques (Superovulation, principles of superovulation, protocols for superovulation in farm livestock) Biotechnological Utilization of Female Reproductive Potential: In Vitro fertilization (IVF) in ruminants; potential uses of IVF. Mechanisms involved in IVF: harvesting and maturation of oocytes; collection and capacitating of sperm; fertilization and development of embryos to a transferable stage. Metablomics and Metabonomics in Animal Biotechnology: Definition, promising areas of applications of metabolomics in livestock production systems. Metabonomics and the impact of dietary components on gene expression and production of metabolites. Transgenic Animal Production and Applications: Methods of transgenic animal production; advantages and limitations of methods; transgenic animal as human disease model; applications of transgenic models and transgenic livestock. Cryobiology: Definition, Importance, principles of cryopreservation, methods of cryopreservation. Sexing of Sperms and Embryos: Sperm sexing, Separation of X and Y chromosome; Cytogenetics of X and Y spersm; Techniques of sperm separation(albumin column, H-Y antigen, Flow sorting by DNA content, Sephadex column); Embryo sexing technique: separation on the basis of sexual dimorphism, fluorescent in situ hybridization, detection of the H-Y antigen, Use of Y specific DNA Probes. Artificial Insemination (AI): Methods of sperm collection, Evaluation of sperm quality in farm animals, Techniques of insemination in livestock and poultry. Merits and demerits of different techniques of Artificial Insemination (AI). Cloning: Definition; history of animal cloning; cloning of mammals. Manipulation of Gametes and Embryos: Evaluation of chromosomes of ova; embryos and zonapellucida; manipulation of gametes. Anatomy and physiology of embryos in relation to micromanipulation; culture methods; dividing embryos. Combining embryonic cells; intracellular manipulation and conservation of manipulated embryos. Peptides in Animal Health: Synthetic peptide production and applications in animal therapeutics; production and applications of monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies. Animal Vaccine Production by Recombinant DNA Technology: Subunit vaccines, attenuated vaccines and vector vaccines for animal’s viral and bacterial diseases.

Rationale of the Course: This course will enable the students to acquire the knowledge about basic knowledge of business and its implications in starting new venture.
Course objectives: This course aimed to
Provide an understanding of the different forms of business, industry and services;
Develop and strengthen entrepreneurial quality, i.e., motivation or need for achievement;
Analyze environmental set up relating to small industry and promoting it; understand the process and procedure involved in setting up small units.
Know the sources of help and support available for starting a small-scale industry.

Pro Forma financial statements- pro forma income statement, pro forma balance sheet, pro forma statement of cash flow. This course will look at how genetics has changed over the years and the effects that this has had to forensic investigation, we will also look at how future advances in genetics might have an impact on future criminals and investigations.

To introduce participants to genetics
